Fatma remains hidden directly behind the father's body
Zoubida's hands clip through the front surface of her haik

Fatma's arm is cut at the right edge of the frame and the background is an empty wall with no stampeding crowd

defects: Fatma still lacks a haik and holds her arms wide apart instead of clutching her garment to her breastbone and looking over her shoulder

tiles.fix: Separate the background runner from Sidi Mohammed's silhouette and pose Fatma clutching a haik to her breastbone while looking back.

defects: The father and the dellal shoving each other at the head of the crowd are obscured/missing behind a small cluster of generic walkers
Crowd characters in the center (the boys in green and blue tunics and the woman in yellow) clip into one another

tiles.fix: Stage the father and the dellal clearly visible at the front shoving up the lane, space out the following crowd to stop mesh interpenetration, and keep the foreground observers/turban consistent.

defects: The receding crowd converges onto the same centerline with multiple characters clipping through each other's bodies
The father and the dellal grappling are not readable at the front of the procession

worst_problem: Key narrative props and costumes contradict the spoken lines and staging: Fatma screams 'Mon haïk !' with arms spread wide while wearing no haik at all, the father keeps his turban on his head during 'Mon père avait perdu son turban', and the father and dellal never actually touch or grip each other's collars during the fight.
